//: Committed, non-secret configuration. SAFE TO COMMIT — and it must STAY that way.
Every key below is an endpoint, a resource name, or a tuning value. None is a
credential. Authentication uses Azure Entra ID via DefaultAzureCredential, so
there is no key or connection string to store in the first place: the strongest
guarantee that a secret is never committed is that the secret does not exist.
Local development : dotnet user-secrets  (stored outside the repo)
Production        : environment variables / Key Vault via managed identity
See CONFIGURATION.md at the repo root.

Chunking.//: Changing these invalidates every chunk already produced — chunk ids derive from position. Treat a change as a corpus rebuild.

//: Telemetry is collected here and exported by the composition root only.
The inner layers instrument themselves through BCL types (ActivitySource,
Meter) and know nothing about OpenTelemetry or Application Insights.
AzureMonitor:ConnectionString is EMPTY on purpose, exactly like every other
endpoint in this file. Supply it by environment variable or Key Vault. It is
not a read credential — it authorises ingestion, not query — but anyone
holding it can write into the workspace, so it does not belong in the repo.
Export authenticates with Entra ID via DefaultAzureCredential; there is no
instrumentation key to rotate.
Observability.//ServiceVersion: Empty uses the assembly's informational version. Set it from the build pipeline to correlate a latency change with the deployment that caused it.
Observability.//SamplingRatio: 1.0 records every trace. Lower it only when volume demands: metrics stay exact at any ratio because they are counted before the sampler runs, so alerting is unaffected. Sampling is parent-based, so a trace already sampled upstream is never dropped mid-path.

Instrumentation.//: Individually switchable because they cost and fail differently.
Instrumentation.//AzureSdk: Turns 'the upload was slow' into 'the third indexing batch was throttled and retried twice'. The Azure SDKs suppress their inner HTTP spans while this is on, so it does not duplicate HttpClient instrumentation.

Otlp.//: For a local collector — the Aspire dashboard, Jaeger, a sidecar — so spans are visible on a laptop without an Azure resource. Empty disables it.

HealthChecks.//: Bound in Infrastructure, which owns the dependency checks. Liveness never contacts a dependency; only readiness does.
HealthChecks.//TimeoutSeconds: A readiness probe that hangs is worse than one that fails: the orchestrator waits, and the instance is neither serving nor restarted.
HealthChecks.//CacheSeconds: Bounds how often probes reach Azure. Uncached, every orchestrator poll on every instance becomes a billed request that counts toward the same throttling limits as real traffic — and readiness then fails hardest exactly when the dependency is already struggling.
HealthChecks.//ExposeDetails: Off by default: a detailed body enumerates this service's dependencies and which one is broken, to anyone who can reach an endpoint that probes cannot authenticate to. Turn on only when the endpoint is restricted.

Credential.//: Empty ManagedIdentityClientId = system-assigned identity. Set only for user-assigned. Not a secret.

Storage.//: Account URI, not a connection string. Connection strings embed a key; URIs do not.

Search.//index: Two indexes, two granularities. IndexName is keyed by document and answers 'which documents exist'. ChunkIndexName is keyed by chunk and answers 'which passages match'.
Search.//batching: The 16MB request ceiling binds before Azure's 1000-document limit: a 3072-dim vector is roughly 40KB of JSON, so 100 chunks is about 4MB.
Search.//hnsw: HnswM and HnswEfConstruction are fixed at index creation; changing them requires a rebuild and reload. HnswEfSearch can be revised in place.
Search.//vectorizer: Service-side Azure OpenAI vectorizer: disabled and not used. The application generates query embeddings itself and submits a VectorizedQuery, so the search service needs no identity or role on AI Foundry.

DocumentIntelligence.//: Empty Endpoint selects the local PdfPig extractor. Set it to enable OCR of scanned documents.

AiFoundry.//chat: Answers hitting the token ceiling are returned truncated and logged. For a reasoning model the ceiling includes its reasoning tokens.
AiFoundry.//ChatTemperature: Absent on purpose: no temperature is sent and the model's default applies. Reasoning models (gpt-5-mini) reject any other value with 400. For a non-reasoning model set 0.0 for reproducible answers.
AiFoundry.//model: The model the embedding deployment serves. For a known model, EmbeddingDimensions is checked against it at startup.
AiFoundry.//: The model's native output length, and the dimension knowledge-chunks is created with. Changing it means recreating that index and re-ingesting.
AiFoundry.//batching: Chunks per embedding request. The binding limit is tokens per request, not items — an 800-character chunk is roughly 200 tokens.
AiFoundry.//retry: Owned by Polly; the SDK's own retry is disabled so the two cannot multiply. RetryMaxDelaySeconds also caps any server-supplied Retry-After. Shared by embeddings, chat, and the agent — one resource, one quota, one budget.

//: The Foundry agent.
ProjectEndpoint is REQUIRED (empty here like every other endpoint; the
host refuses to start without it): https://<account>.services.ai.azure.com/api/projects/<project>.
Chat and embeddings are served at the account; agents only at a project.
The account endpoint answers 404 to agent calls, so there is no fallback.
Version is REQUIRED outside Development. A pinned version is verified on
first use: its stored definition fingerprint must match this build's
(instructions, tool schema, model deployment, temperature), or the agent
route fails rather than run a different agent. Empty is allowed only in
Development, where the process provisions a matching version on the
first question and logs the number to pin.
Agent.Name: knowledge-assistant
Agent.//model: Empty reuses ChatDeploymentName. Separable because the agent must decide what to search for, which a smaller model does noticeably worse than it writes prose.
Agent.//Temperature: Absent on purpose, as ChatTemperature: left out of the agent definition so the model's default applies. With a non-reasoning model set 0.0 — temperature also perturbs what the agent decides to search for. Part of the definition fingerprint, so changing it needs a newly pinned version.
Agent.//MaxToolIterations: The hard cost ceiling. An agent decides for itself when it has searched enough; this bounds how long it may keep deciding 'not yet', each round costing a completion and a retrieval. Reaching it is logged and the agent is asked to answer with what it has, not failed.
Agent.//MaxSearchResultCharacters: Backstop on one search's payload, the counterpart of the retrieval pipeline's context budget. Passages arrive in rank order, so trimming drops the least relevant.
